questions.question: A and B are in ideal condition. The ratio of molecular weights of A and B is 1 : 4. The pressure of the gas mixture of A and B with equal weight is P atm. What is the partial pressure (in atm) of mixture B?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P/5.**__

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Daltons Law of Partial Pressure:**

 
 
• The total pressure of Gas exerted is the** sum of partial pressure exerted by all gases. **
 
• Pₜₒₜₐₗ = P₁ + P₂ + P₃
 
 
 
• For two gases in the container, the r**elationship between the partial pressure of a gas (Pa) and the total pressure is given as **

Pₐ = (n_a)/(n_a + n_b) PTₒₜₐₗ ----(1)

 
• Pa is the partial pressure of first gas, nₐ is the number of moles of gas A and nb is the number of moles of gas B. 

**Calculation:**__

 
• Given the ratio of molecular weight is 1 : 4
 
 
• or Mₐ = 4 Mb ----(2)
 
 
 
• Their weight is the same, so mass is same
 
 
• Wₐ = Wb = W -- (3)
 
 
 
• Now, the number of moles is given by mass / molecular mass
 
• Number of moles of a
 
 
• n_a = (W_a)/(M_a) = (W)/(M_a) ----(4)
 
 
 
• Number of moles of b
 
 
• n_b= (W_b)/(M_b) = (W)/(M_b) ----(5)
 
 
 
• Now partial pressure of B from the equation 1
 
 
• Pb = (n_b)/(n_a + n_b) PTₒₜₐₗ ----(6)
 
 
 
• Putting (4) and (5) in 6
 
 
• Pb = (W/M_b)/(W/M_a + W/M_b) PTₒₜₐₗ ----(7)
 
 
 
• Now putting (2) in 7
 
• Pb = (W/M_b)/(W/4M_b + W/M_b) PTₒₜₐₗ
 
• implies P_b = (1)/((1+4)) PTₒₜₐₗ
 
• implies P_b = frac{PTₒₜₐₗ}{5}
 
• **So, (P)/(5) is the correct option.**

questions.question: There are two pipes, pipe M and pipe N to fill a tank. Pipe M alone can fill {2}over{3} of the empty tank's capacity in 24 hours. Pipe N alone can fill {5}over{6} of the empty tank's capacity in 60 hours. Both pipes fill water at their respective rates. How many hours will both pipes fill the empty tank together according to their capacity?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe M alone can fill (2)/(3) of the empty tank's capacity in 24 hours

Pipe N alone can fill (5)/(6) of the empty tank's capacity in in 60 hours

**Formula Used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Pipe M can fill 2/3 of empty tank in 24 hours 

⇒ Pipe M can fill the complete tank = (24 × 3)/2 hours

⇒ Pipe M can fill the complete tank = 36 hours 

Pipe N can fill 5/6 of empty tank in 60 hours

⇒ Pipe N can fill the complete tank = (60 × 6)/5 hours

⇒ Pipe N can fill the complete tank = 72 hours 

Total work = LCM of M's Time and N's Time 

LCM of 36 and 72 = 72 hours

Efficiency of M = 72/36 = 2 

Efficiency of N = 72/72 = 1 

Time taken by M & N together = 72/3 

⇒ 24 hours

**∴ Both pipes will fill the empty tank together according to their capacity in 24 hours.**

questions.solution:

• **Momentum = mass*velocity.**
 
• **Vector **quantities are those which have **direction **as well as **magnitude**.
 
• **Scalar** quantities are those which have only **magnitude**.
 
• **Momentum **has also **direction **along with **magnitude**.
 
• **Kinetic energy** has no direction it has only **magnitude**.

questions.question: Some long circular cylindrical small chocolates were made by a cylindrical chocolate having base radius 6 cm and height 6cm. The radius of base of each small chocolate is 2 cm and height is 2 cm. If the small chocolates are placed in 9 × 3 configuration in a rectangular box and the height of the box is 2 cm, Find the percentage of free space inside the box based on volume? (use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cylindrical chocolate dimensions: Radius = 6 cm and Height = 6 cm

Long small cylindrical chocolate dimensions: Radius = 2 cm and Height = 2 cm

Rectangular box dimensions: Height = 2 cm

Small cylindrical chocolates are placed in 9 × 3 configuration

 **Formula Used:**

Volume of cylinder = π(Radius)²(height)

Volume of cylindrical chocolate = number of small cylindrical chocolate × Volume of a small cylindrical chocolate

Volume of rectangular box = length × breadth × height

Percentage = (value/total value) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let n be number of small cylindrical chocolates

Volume of cylindrical chocolate = π(6 cm)²(6 cm)

⇒ Volume of cylindrical chocolate = 216π cm³

Volume of a small cylindrical chocolate = π(2 cm)²(2 cm)

⇒ Volume of a small cylindrical chocolate = 8π cm³

216π cm³ = n × 8π cm³

⇒ n = 216π/8π 

⇒ n = 27

Each small cylindrical chocolate is placed in 9 × 3 configurations in the box 

⇒ Along length 9 small cylindrical chocolates are placed and along width 3 small cylindrical chocolates are placed

**⇒ Dimensions of the box:**

Length = 9 × diameter of a small cylindrical chocolate

and width = 3 × diameter of a small cylindrical ball

⇒ Length = 9 × 4 cm = 36 cm 

⇒ Width = 3 × 4 cm = 12 cm 

Volume of Rectangular box = 36 × 12 × 2 cm³

⇒ Volume of Rectangular box = 864 cm³

Volume of all the small cylindrical chocolate = 27 × 8π cm³ 

⇒ 216π cm³

⇒ Volume of all the small cylindrical chocolates = 678.24 cm³

Free space in the rectangular box based on volume = Volume of Rectangular box – Volume of all the small cylindrical chocolates

⇒ Free space in the rectangular box based on volume = 864 – 678.24 = 185.76 cm³

Percentage of free space = (185.76/864) × 100

⇒ 21.5%

**∴ 21.5% free space inside the box based on volume**

questions.question: If the intensity of the rustle of the leaves is 10⁻¹¹ Wm⁻², what will be the level of intensity due to that rustle?

**The rustling of the leaves:**

__
 
• A **rustling** is a gentle swishing sound, like the **rustling **of leaves in the **trees **on a **breezy **night. 
 
• The rustling happens when the wind blows. Small speed differences in the airflow on either side of the **leaf** create vortices that detach from the **leaf** surface, lowering the pressure on one side and **causing** it to flutter.

Sound Intensity: It is also known as acoustic intensity.

 
• It is the power carried by sound waves per unit area in a direction perpendicular to that area.
 
• The sound intensity level is just a logarithmic expression of sound intensity relative to a reference intensity. Mathematically

L = 10log₁₀(I)/(I₀)

where L is the Level of the sound intensity, I is the intensity of the sound intensity, and I0 is the reference intensity.

I0 = 10-12 w/m².

**Calculations__:**

Given that, I = 10¹¹ Wm⁻², I0 = 10⁻¹² w/m².

So by the sound intensity,

L = 10log₁₀(I)/(I₀) = 10log₁₀frac{10⁻¹¹}{10⁻¹²} = 10 Db

**So the level of intensity due to that rustle is 10 Db.**

questions.question: Two people are cycling at the speed of 10.8 km/h and 12 km/h, a bus running in the same direction crosses the cyclist in 9 seconds and 13.5 seconds respectively. What is the length of the bus?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two people are cycling at a speed of 10.8 km/hr and 12 km/hr, and in the same direction, a bus is also traveling. The bus crosses two people in 9 and 13.5 seconds.

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/ Time

1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s

Concept used:

When they are moving in the same direction, the relative speed between the two bodies is the difference of their speeds,

(u – v) if u > v

(v – u) if v > u.

**Calculation:**

Let us assume the speed of the Bus = B km/hr, L m be the length of the bus.

Now the distance traveled by two people while Bus crosses them is the length of the Bus.

⇒ (L) m = (B – 10.8) × 9 × 5/18 = (B – 12) × 13.5 × 5/18 

⇒ (B – 10.8) × 9 = (B – 12)× 13.5

⇒ 2× (B – 10.8) = 3× (B – 12)

⇒ 2B – 21.6 = 3B – 36

⇒ 36 – 21.6 = 3B – 2B

⇒ B = 14.4 Km/hr

Now the length of the bus L m will be

∴ (14.4 – 12) × 13.5 × 5/18 = 9

 When **two objects interact**, they apply forces to each other of **equal magnitude** and **opposite direction.**
